content.title: About
content.content: Almond flour is made from finely ground almonds. It is a gluten‑free product with a subtle nutty aroma, commonly used in baking, desserts, and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almond flour is suitable for gluten‑free diets.
It contains more protein and healthy fats than wheat flour.
Almond flour can replace part or all of wheat flour in recipes, giving a moister crumb.
When stored in the fridge or freezer it stays fresh longer.
It is a staple in keto and paleo kitchens.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Almond fats support heart health and help maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Protein and fiber promote satiety and support digestive health.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium is important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: People with nut allergies may react to almond flour.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Almond flour is calorie‑dense, so it should be used in moderation.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Those prone to kidney stones should limit intake due to oxalates.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Almond flour can be added to baked goods, pancakes, muffins, cookies, sauces, and breadings. It blends well with other gluten‑free flours. For a lighter texture, sift it before use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store almond flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
